items.summary: fix(gateway): stop deferred agent admission from queueing behind other agents (#165107) Deferred startup recovery chained every agent's whole preparation (secrets refresh, session migration, model refresh) through one FIFO, so a 12 MB agent waited ~36 minutes behind two slower agents on a starved Gateway, and nothing was logged between deferral and recovery. Open and session migration now run per agent (two open slots, four migration slots, readiness awaited without a slot). Only credential/model publication and final admission keep the FIFO turn, with the existing config, revision, auth-store, model and deletion checks. Migration uses the same agent-database configuration guard as the open step. Recovery and degraded lines now carry elapsedMs and phaseDurationsMs, and a 60 s progress warning names each pending agent's phase and, while waiting for publication, the agent holding the turn.

items.title: improve: native tool rows show Tool Search calls and every client sha…
items.summary: improve: native tool rows show Tool Search calls and every client shares tool icons (#165095) * fix(apps): show Tool Search tool_call rows as the called tool in native chat With Tool Search enabled, the model invokes tools through the `tool_call` dispatcher (`{ id, args }`). #163829 taught the Control UI and shared TS display to render these as the called tool; the native apps still showed a bare "Tool Call" row with no detail. Apply the same presentation-only unwrap at each native display owner: - Swift: ToolDisplayRegistry.displayCall (OpenClawKit) maps tool_call to the called tool (catalog ids openclaw|mcp|client:: resolve to the tool name; plain names pass through; inner args only when they are an object). resolve() applies it, and the chat row uses it for title, detail, icon, diff, and result formatting. macOS work-activity kind and the iOS Live Activity tool name use the display name. The transcript cache keeps only the dispatcher id (plus inner patch input) so cache-restored rows still render the called tool. - Android: unwrapToolCallForDisplay projects ChatToolActivity name, detail, and arguments for history rows and live rows. Execution identity stays raw: toolCallId, stored transcript names, pending live call state, merge/presentation keys, outcomes, approvals, and result extraction (browser tabs, web_search source previews). tool-display.json is unchanged. * refactor(tools): replace tool emoji with shared semantic icons Graphical clients had already moved from tool emoji to icons, but the emoji stayed the source of truth: the Control UI picked its SVG by mapping each tool's emoji through a hand-written table (about 45 of 71 tools fell through to the puzzle), Swift guessed SF Symbols from name substrings, and Android showed a generic list glyph for most tools. Text surfaces still prefixed emoji. The shared tool display config now owns tool iconography: every tool and the fallback carry an `icon`, a semantic name from the Control UI icon set, and `emoji` is gone. tool-display.json is regenerated from the config. - Web reads `icon` directly; the emoji-to-icon and name-override tables are deleted (five foreign alias names translate to canonical tools). Row-kind icons and plugin activity icons keep their precedence. 45 tools that showed a puzzle now get real icons; existing visuals are unchanged. - Swift (OpenClawKit/ChatUI) decodes `icon` and maps it through one SF Symbol table with the web row-kind precedence, replacing the substring heuristic. Android reads the bundled asset once and maps it through one Material table. Each platform has a test asserting every config icon has a glyph. - Text surfaces drop the pictograph: channel progress drafts (Telegram, Slack, Discord, Matrix, Feishu, ...), ACP summaries, tool-meta aggregates, and the TUI now read like `Exec: pnpm test`. The plugin SDK ChannelProgressDraftLine.icon field is unchanged; core no longer sets it, so plain renderers use their existing bullet. - Status reactions are emoji by nature and keep their exact per-tool reaction emoji through a reaction-owned table, no longer coupled to tool display. Docs updated for the plain progress rows and semantic icons. * test(channels): align gateway progress assertions with plain tool labels * test(discord): align consolidated progress expectations Preserve the plain tool labels when main consolidates progress cases into the final-draft suite. * fix(ui): narrow shared tool icon names with a type guard
